prompt: What does the Glue Data Catalog hold about Quitanda's orders?
hint: Delete every object and look again.

choices.text: A copy of the Parquet files, kept in Glue's own storage for speed
choices.why: The catalog keeps no data; the files stay in S3 and only there.

choices.text: The columns, the location, the format and the partitions
choices.why: Right: a description that every reader by name consults before reading a byte.

choices.text: The results of the latest queries, kept for reuse
choices.why: Athena writes results to an S3 prefix; the catalog never sees them.

choices.text: An index of every `order_id`, for lookups
choices.why: Nothing in the catalog knows a value inside a file; it refused a filter on `payment` for that reason.

prompt: Somebody deletes every object under `s3://quitanda-curated-prod/orders/`. What happens to the table `orders` in the catalog?
hint: Two facts in two services.

choices.text: It is deleted with the objects
choices.why: S3 does not tell the catalog anything; the table stays.

choices.text: It is marked deprecated straight away
choices.why: Only a crawler with that delete behaviour marks tables, and only when it runs.

choices.text: It rolls back to its previous version
choices.why: Versions change only with `update-table`.

choices.text: Nothing: it stays, and queries return no rows
choices.why: Right. The description outlives the files it describes.

prompt: Match each part of a table to the question it answers.
hint: Look at `orders-table.json`.

pairs.right: What is in each file, with which type
Which columns come from the key

right_distractors: Who is allowed to read the table

prompt: `orders-table.json` lists seven columns. Suppose a file in the location had only six. At what point would anybody find out?
hint: What did `create-table` read?

choices.text: At `create-table`, which compares the columns with the files
choices.why: It reads only the JSON it was sent; neither moto nor AWS opens a file.

choices.text: When a query reads that file through the table
choices.why: Right. A table is a claim about the files, and only a reader puts the two side by side.

choices.text: At the next nightly check the catalog makes of every location
choices.why: The catalog makes no such check.

choices.text: When the file is written, because S3 validates Parquet
choices.why: S3 stores bytes and does not know what format they are.

prompt: What does one partition of `orders` hold?
hint: It is a row in the catalog.

choices.text: The day's Parquet file, copied in from S3 when the row is made
choices.why: The file is in S3; the partition only says where.

choices.text: A value of `dt` and a storage descriptor with its own location
choices.why: Right, columns and format included, copied from the table when it was made.

choices.text: The number of orders that day
choices.why: The catalog does not count rows; a Parquet footer does.

choices.text: A link to the partition of the day before, so they can be walked in order
choices.why: Partitions are independent rows found by their values.

prompt: `batch-create-partition` takes up to 100 partitions per request. How many requests register a year of 365 daily partitions?
hint: Round up.

prompt: Sent a second time, the batch answered with 31 errors and exit status 0. What should the nightly job that registers its day do about that?
hint: What does the exit status say?

choices.text: Trust the exit status, which says the call succeeded
choices.why: It was 0 with 31 failures inside the answer.

choices.text: Read the `Errors` list and act on each entry
choices.why: Right. `AlreadyExistsException` is harmless; any other code is a day not registered.

choices.text: Delete every partition first, so that the batch never meets one
choices.why: For the length of that window every query sees an empty table.

choices.text: Retry the batch until the list of errors comes back empty
choices.why: An existing partition fails the same way on every retry.

prompt: `get-partitions --expression "payment = 'pix'"` was refused with `Invalid partition expression`. Why?
hint: What does the catalog know about `payment`?

choices.text: moto does not evaluate partition expressions, whatever column they name
choices.why: It evaluated the `dt BETWEEN` one and returned three rows.

choices.text: It names a column inside the files, and the catalog knows only the keys
choices.why: Right. The catalog knows values of `dt` and nothing of what the files hold.

choices.text: The value has to be written in double quotes
choices.why: The `dt` expression used single quotes and worked.

choices.text: `pix` is not one of the values the table declares for `payment`, so nothing matches
choices.why: A table declares types, not values.

prompt: A partition for `2026-12-25` names a prefix that holds no objects. What does an Athena query for that day return?
hint: Nothing ties the row to the files.

choices.text: An error saying that the location does not exist
choices.why: A prefix is not a thing that exists or not; listing it finds nothing, and that is not an error.

choices.text: The whole table, because the filter matched no files
choices.why: The filter picked one partition; it does not fall back to all of them.

choices.text: No rows, and no error
choices.why: Right. An empty prefix is an empty answer, which is why a row with no files goes unnoticed.

choices.text: Nothing, because the catalog refused to create that row
choices.why: It accepted it; the capture listed `2026-12-25` straight after.

prompt: Which of these count as objects against the catalog's free million? Choose all that apply.
hint: An object is something the catalog stores.

choices.text: The database `quitanda`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The partition for 2026-10-15
choices.why: Yes, each of the 31.

choices.text: Version 2 of the table
choices.why: Yes: a version is a whole table description.

choices.text: The Parquet file of 15 October
choices.why: That is in S3, priced as S3 storage.

choices.text: An Athena query that reads the table
choices.why: A query makes requests, the other free million.

prompt: Why does this lesson's crawler set `UpdateBehavior=LOG` instead of the default?
hint: What does the default do when a file disagrees with the table?

choices.text: A crawl that only logs its findings is billed at a lower DPU rate
choices.why: The DPU-hour is the same; the setting decides what it writes.

choices.text: `CRAWL_NEW_FOLDERS_ONLY` refuses to run with the default
choices.why: The two settings are independent.

choices.text: So one bad export cannot rewrite the table for every query
choices.why: Right. With `UPDATE_IN_DATABASE` the change lands in the catalog the moment the crawl sees it.

choices.text: The default deletes a table whose files changed
choices.why: Deleting is the delete behaviour, and its default only marks a table deprecated.

prompt: The crawler's schedule is `cron(30 3 * * ? *)`. What time is that in São Paulo, three hours behind UTC?
hint: Glue writes schedules in UTC.

choices.why: That reads the expression as local time.
That adds the three hours instead of taking them away.
Right, which may be before the night's export has landed.
The 3 is the hour of a 24-hour clock.

prompt: A crawler runs over a prefix where one day's folder holds files with a different set of columns from the rest. What can it make of that?
hint: It groups by how similar the schemas are.

choices.text: A table for each folder instead of one table with partitions
choices.why: Right, unless it is told to keep a single schema for the path.

choices.text: It refuses to run until the odd files are removed
choices.why: A crawler does not refuse; it infers and writes what it inferred.

choices.text: It rewrites the odd files to match the other folders
choices.why: A crawler writes the catalog and never the data.

choices.text: It skips that folder and leaves no trace of it in the catalog
choices.why: Skipping silently is not what grouping does; differing schemas change how it groups.

prompt: A crawl is billed at 0.69 dollars per DPU-hour, per second, with a ten-minute minimum. A run takes 3 minutes on 2 DPUs. How many US cents does it cost?
hint: The minimum applies before the DPUs multiply.

prompt: Before it infers a schema, a crawler tries its ___ in order, each one saying whether a file is its format.
hint: Custom ones can go first: a grok pattern, a delimiter of its own.

prompt: After `update-table` adds `coupon`, what do the 31 partitions of October list as their columns?
hint: What did each partition copy when it was made?

choices.text: The eight columns, since partitions follow the table
choices.why: The capture shows 15 October still ending in `neighbourhood`.

choices.text: The seven they were created with
choices.why: Right. `update-table` changes the table and none of its partitions.

choices.text: None: an update clears their columns until a crawl runs
choices.why: Nothing is cleared; the partitions are untouched.

choices.text: Whatever version 1 of the table says, read at query time
choices.why: A partition holds its own copy, not a pointer to a version.

prompt: `update-table --skip-archive` left a fourth version in moto. What does the flag do on AWS?
hint: moto ignored it.

choices.text: It updates the table without archiving the previous description
choices.why: Right, so the version count stays put; moto does not implement it.

choices.text: It archives the table and skips the update
choices.why: The update happens; what is skipped is the archive.

choices.text: It deletes every earlier version to make room
choices.why: Earlier versions are left alone.

choices.text: It skips updating the partitions along with the table, which it otherwise does
choices.why: `update-table` never updates partitions, with or without the flag.

prompt: Version 3 made `total_cents` a `double`, and you want the table back as it was in version 2. How?
hint: A version is a whole description.

choices.text: Delete version 3, and the table falls back to version 2
choices.why: The current description is the table itself, not an archived version to delete.

choices.text: Run a crawler with `UpdateBehavior=LOG`
choices.why: LOG only stops a crawler from changing the table; it restores nothing.

choices.text: Rewrite the 31 partitions as `double`
choices.why: That changes the partitions to match the mistake.

choices.text: Send `update-table` with version 2's description
choices.why: Right, which makes a version 4 equal to version 2: the history keeps the mistake and the undo.

prompt: `ask.py` refused `coupon` although the file of 1 November has that column. Why?
hint: Whose schema was in charge?

choices.text: The catalog's version 1 has no `coupon`
choices.why: `ask.py` never reads the catalog; it lists S3.

choices.text: PyArrow took the schema from the first file, 1 October
choices.why: Right. The reader decided the schema, and it decided from October.

choices.text: A column that holds nulls on most of its rows cannot be counted
choices.why: `count(coupon)` counts the non-null values, which is what the union query did.

choices.text: `coupons.py` wrote the column under another name
choices.why: DuckDB found `coupon` in the same file once told to unite by name.

prompt: In the file of 2 November a total of exactly 52.00 reais is stored in `total_cents` as a `double`. Read with October's `int64` schema, what does it become?
hint: The refusal came from a value with centavos.

choices.text: An error, as there was for the total of 265.68
choices.why: The error came because 265.68 has a fraction to lose; 52.00 has none.

choices.text: 5,200 cents, converted correctly
choices.why: Nothing multiplies by a hundred; the reader only changes the type.

choices.text: 52, read as fifty-two cents, with no error
choices.why: Right: the silent case, a hundred times too small.

choices.text: A null, because the two types disagree with each other
choices.why: The value converts cleanly, so nothing becomes null.

prompt: With `union_by_name = true`, what did DuckDB answer for the `coupon` of the 31 October rows?
hint: 60,725 orders, 5,982 with a coupon.

choices.text: An error, since that file has no such column
choices.why: The error was the query without `union_by_name`.

choices.text: NULL for every one of them
choices.why: Right: lined up by name, a column a file lacks comes back empty.

choices.text: The coupon of the matching order in November
choices.why: A union lines up columns, not rows; nothing is matched across files.

choices.text: An empty string in place of each coupon
choices.why: `count(coupon)` counted 5,982, all from November, which an empty string would have raised.

prompt: The raw CSV table is read by position. The export adds `channel` between `payment` and `neighbourhood`, and the table is updated to match. What do the old October files show?
hint: Count the fields of an old line.

choices.text: Every column as before, with `channel` empty
choices.why: That is what reading by name would give; by position the fields shift.

choices.text: An error on every old line, which has one field too few
choices.why: A short line is read with the missing field empty, not refused.

choices.text: The old seventh field lands in the new column, and the last one is empty
choices.why: Right. The seventh field lands in the seventh column, which is now `channel`.

choices.text: Nothing, until a crawler updates the partitions
choices.why: The files are readable at once; they are read wrong.

prompt: Put in order a safe change of `total_cents` from cents to reais.
hint: A type changes by adding a column.
items: The export starts filling `total_reais` on new days
A job rewrites the old partitions with `total_reais`

prompt: Of the four ways to add partitions, which one needs no partition rows in the catalog at all?
hint: Lesson 15 described it.

choices.text: `MSCK REPAIR TABLE`
choices.why: It lists the prefix and writes the rows it finds missing.

choices.text: A crawler with `CRAWL_NEW_FOLDERS_ONLY`
choices.why: It writes rows for the new folders.

choices.text: Partition projection
choices.why: Right: Athena computes the keys from the table's properties.

choices.text: `batch-create-partition` from the writer
choices.why: That is writing the rows yourself.
